title: Colonels upend unbeaten Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonels upend unbeaten Queen Anne's

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 953
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Makayla Newcomb has pitched well this season.But Colonel Richardson High's softball team either couldn't deliver the big hit or make the big play defensively when it was needed.
Tuesday, the Colonels got both.
Aubrey Taylor ripped a two-run triple down the right-field line and Newcomb crafted a complete-game five-hitter, as the Colonels defeated Queen Anne's County, 4-1, dealing the Lions their first loss of the season.
"She's had a good year for us," Colonel Richardson head coach Brett Ireland said of Newcomb (7-4), who finished with 10 strikeouts and no walks. "All year we just couldn't make enough plays or one thing would go wrong and it sort of snowballed. But we got the clutch hit today. We've struggled with the runners in scoring position."
Colonel (7-4 overall, 2-2 North Bayside) took a 1-0 lead in the first inning, as Kylie Rhinehardt, Clarissa Peugh, Eileen Johnson and Tyla Dickerson each singled off Hannah Martin (6-1), with Dickerson's hit to center plating Rhinehardt.
Martin though prevented the big inning, retiring the next three batters to end the inning, then setting down the side in order in the second.
Martin issued her only walk of the game to Peugh to lead off the third. Johnson (2 for 3) singled to left. Peugh was forced at third when Dickerson bounced into a fielder's choice. Taylor (2 for 3) then laced a 1-0 offering down the right-field line, scoring Johnson and Dickerson. Taylor raced home on an overthrow to third.
"Mostly I was just looking for a hit to the right side because I knew it would score both the runs on first and second," Taylor said.
That's exactly what her coach was looking for as well.
"Aubrey stepped up today and gave us a big hit," Ireland said. "Runners on first and second, she hit a triple down the line. I was hoping someone would hit it down that far just because I could see the right fielder was in right-center a lot. That (right-field) line was open and once it got there both runs were able to score. And Aubrey made good hustle to third. And then there was an overthrow and (she) was able to get in there and score. That really gave us nice comfortable lead. I was wishing we could tack on more but we just couldn't do it."
Martin yielded only one more hit the rest of the way, retiring 13 of the final 15 batters she faced.
"I think Hannah pitched extremely well," Queen Anne's head coach Aaron Stewart said, whose pitcher allowed seven hits and struck out seven. "Four runs. Our average is eight, nine runs. We score eight, nine runs — we had that one bad inning — we win the game."
Newcomb held the Lions (9-1, 2-1) to their lowest run total of the season and retired the first nine batters she faced before Queen Anne's scored its lone run in the fourth.
"I had a little bit of pressure, but I just go on top of the hitters," Newcomb said. "Once I got three-up, three-down on the whole lineup the first time (I was good). My curveball was good. And just the fastball, spotting it."
Newcomb recorded five of her 10 strikeouts through the first three innings.
That streak ended in the fourth, when Cam Jacobi drove a leadoff double to the fence in left field. Caroline Taylor then hit a line drive that Peugh made a diving stop on at second base. Autumn Huber followed with another double to the left-field fence, scoring Jacobi to make it 4-1.
But Newcomb got Abbie Denes and Martin to fly out to end the inning.
"Makayla threw a great game today," Ireland said. "She hit her spots well. We know Queen Anne's has some good sticks and I thought she was able to throw her off-speed pitch for strikes and got a couple of big outs with that. I thought the second and third time through the lineup, the changeup was good enough to get us some outs. "
Queen Anne's threatened again in the fifth.
Emily Rendulic stroked a single just over the outstretched glove of Taylor at short. Newcomb got a called third strike on Morgan Gottleib. Emilie Smith then doubled into the left-field corner, moving Rendulic to third. But Newcomb stifled the rally there, notching a strikeout and before inducing an inning-ending pop-up.
"We couldn't hit the ball today," Stewart said. "That's what it pretty much came down to. We've hit the ball extremely, extremely well all year long and we just couldn't get the hit today. Looked like she (Newcomb) was throwing the good stuff and we couldn't hit the ball. We normally put up eight, nine runs every game and one run isn't going to win you games. But we move on."
NORTH DORCHESTER 4, EASTON 1EASTON — Emilee Cohee hurled a two-hitter, striking out 14 and walking none, as the Eagles took over sole possession of first place in the North Bayside.
Mackenzie Lewis and freshmen Kinsley Peters and Journey Pearson each had two hits for the Eagles (9-0, 3-0), who ended Easton's three-game win streak.
BASEBALLST. MICHAELS 10, CAMBRIDGE-SD 0CAMBRIDGE — Connor Wheeler went 3 for 3 with a double and a stolen base, and Jacob Bealefeld tossed a three-hitter, striking out six and walking one, as the Saints blanked the Vikings in five innings.
Bealefeld went 2 for 3 with a double and two runs scored, and Henry Mullikin (2 for 3) doubled and drove in two runs for St. Michaels (9-0, 4-0).
COLONEL 5, QUEEN ANNE'S 3CENTREVILLE — Daniel Hesson pitched a complete game, striking out six and yielding no earned runs as Colonel (10-1, 3-0) handed the Lions (7-2, 2-1) their first North Bayside loss.
Jack Walls and Hesson each had two hits for Colonel Richardson. Gavin Whitby added a hit.

title: Easton continues new approach, tops Saints
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton continues new approach, tops Saints

 April 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1079
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — The rough start to the season was one thing.Not making contact though may have troubled Ryan Brice even more. So Easton High's first-year head softball coach tried a different approach.
"I told them, 'We're not going to have any more double-digit strikeout games,'" Brice said. "I told them before each game we're going to line up in the on-deck circle and time the pitcher. I'm not sure, but I think today we only had one strikeout. So I'm going to keep on going with that approach."
That approach certainly worked Monday, as the Warriors churned out 17 hits, including four doubles, on the way to a 14-3 six-inning victory over St. Michaels that extended their win streak to three.
"It's very hard to beat a team like St. Michaels like this," Brice said of a Saints team that entered the game having won three of four, its lone loss coming to defending Class 1A state champion North Dorchester. "They are very well coached. They're very aggressive. They're a good team from top to bottom. So for us to come here and do what we did is huge."
Easton (4-3 overall, 3-0 North Bayside) pushed four runs across in the first inning. Mayah Wilkins (4 for 5) and Lyla Roe (3 for 5) reached on back-to-back singles. Olivia Orrell and Sammy Townsend followed with consecutive run-producing groundouts.
St. Michaels starting pitcher Angel Bock (2-3) looked like she might escape further damage when she worked the count to 1-2 on Laillah Janes. But Janes (2 for 5) singled to right and Gemma Vogel reached on an error before Brynlee Buchkoski (2 for 4) doubled down the left-field line to plate Janes and Vogel for a 4-0 lead.
Myla Ramey relieved Bock to start the second, but Easton stretched its lead to 6-0, scoring two runs on a throwing error.
"Just an off-day all around," St. Michaels head coach David Fisher said after his team slipped to 4-4, 1-2). "I really felt like we were focused and we were ready. We just didn't click. Couple mental errors. It wasn't even the Easton-St. Michaels hype. It was just lack of focus. And then all of a sudden pitching change and we got down early and just didn't pull ourself out."
Easton expanded its lead in the fourth, cranking out five runs on seven hits. Roe reached on an error and scored on Orrell's double down the left-field line to make it 7-0. After Townsend singled, Janes and Vogel delivered consecutive RBI singles for a 9-0 cushion. Isabelle Ludwig added an RBI single before Roe hit a ball deep in the hole at short for an RBI infield hit and an 11-0 lead.
Roe (2-1) had a shutout through four innings, but issued back-to-back walks to Bri Grow and Ramey to open the bottom of the fifth. Roe was relieved by Townsend, who got Katie Jenkins to bounce into a fielder's choice. But Madi White (2 for 3) singled to center, scoring Ramey. Bock followed with a single to right that plated Jenkins before White scored on Lola Browning's sacrifice fly to left, drawing the Saints within 11-3. Townsend stopped the threat there, inducing Brooke Reilly into an inning-ending groundout.
"She pitched a great game," Brice said of Roe, who allowed two runs, three hits, three walks and struck out three over four innings. "I call her a dog for a reason. She's a tough one. Lyla Roe did an amazing job today."
The Warriors regained their 11-run edge in the sixth. Leigha Bosley lined a leadoff double to left. After a Wilkins single, Roe singled to right, scoring Bosley. Wilkins scored on a wild pitch before Townsend's groundout to short plated Roe for a 14-3 lead.
Mercy Haddaway reached on an infield hit to open the Saints' sixth, but Townsend recorded a strikeout before getting a pair of groundouts to second to end the game.
COLONEL 6 CAMBRIDGE-SD 1AMERICAN CORNER — Makayla Newcomb pitched a one-hitter, striking out 11 and walking just one, as the Colonels ended a four-game skid.
Newcomb also had a two-run single for Colonel Richardson (6-4). Montana Davis hit a two-run triple, Sadie Prettyman belted an RBI triple, and Aubrey Taylor cracked a double.
QUEEN ANNE'S 16 KENT COUNTY 0WORTON — Emily Hirschbock had three hits, including a two-run triple and a two-run double as the Lions remained unbeaten.
Hirschbock also earned the win, pitching five innings of three-hit shutout ball. She struck out seven and walked two.
Camaryn Jacobi had three hits for Queen Anne's, and Caroline Taylor and Emily Rendulic had multiple hit games.
BASEBALLST. MICHAELS 3 EASTON 2ST. MICHAELS — Senior left-hander Jacob Seek allowed no earned runs and five hits over 6 2/3 innings to help the Saints remain unbeaten on Monday.
Seek struck out 12 and walked one. Will Sherwood earned the save.
Anthony Massaro was 2 for 3 with a two-run double, and Jacob Bealefeld was 1 for 2 with an RBI and a run scored.
NORTH DORCHESTER 8 KENT ISLAND 5SHILOH — Nate Swann was 2 for 3 with two RBIs and a run scored, and Wes Windsor reached base three times which included an RBI double to fuel the Eagles.
Vernon Price had an RBI double and TJ Leonard and Blake Bramble each scored twice. Boyle also got the save.
COLONEL 10 CAMBRIDGE-SD 0AMERICAN CORNER — Kenton Robbins yielded one hit over 3 2/3 innings, striking out four, as the Colonels blanked the Vikings.
Jack Walls had two hits for Colonel Richardson, and Jordan Regulski, Caleb Rouser, Manny Wallace, Derrick Mitchell and Preston Rickwood each had one hit.
GIRLS LACROSSENORTH CAROLINE 20 EASTON 11RIDGELY — Riley Walstrum (two assists), Reece Bisesi and Claire Blue each had four goals Monday to lead the Bulldogs.
Ashley Kercheval netted a hat trick for North Caroline (3-1) and Ashlynn Bisesi had two goals and two assists. Gracie Faulkner, Calleigh Tribbett and Maddie McNinch had one goal each, and Maddie Nicholson had an assist.
SSPP 21, PALLOTTI 4EASTON — Senior Morgan Quade dished nine assists and scored four goals, and sophomore Eden Zimmerman had four goals and two assists to pace the Sabres.

title: Mardela blanks ND in clash of unbeatens
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Mardela blanks ND in clash of unbeatens

 April 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 691
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SHILOH — This was act one in a potential three-part series.If acts two and three do materialize, North Dorchester High head softball coach Carol Hubbard hopes they go a lot better than this one.
Mardela cranked out 14 hits and sophomore pitcher Hayden Adkins hurled a complete-game one-hitter for her sixth shutout of the season Thursday, as the Warriors rolled to a 10-0 victory over the Eagles in a battle of unbeatens.
"Definitely an off-day," Hubbard said after the Eagles committed an uncharacteristic six errors. "We knew going in we're both tough teams. We both have strong pitching. We both typically put the bat on the ball. Tonight they outplayed us. No other way to say it. We had errors in the field. We didn't put the bat on the ball nearly as well as we're capable of. It just wasn't our day."
Mardela (12-0) took a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Eagles ace Emilee Cohee (5-1). Lexie Guy led off by blooping a single into center field. Julia Wisk advanced her with a sacrifice bunt. Camryn Dorr reached on an error that pushed Guy to third. Ava Twilley hit a comebacker to the mound that Cohee fielded. Knowing she didn't have time to get Guy at the plate, Cohee wisely threw for first for the second out. Karsyn Shockley then smacked a 2-2 pitch to the right-field fence for a double, plating Dorr. Cohee got Elana Donalds to ground out to second, ending the inning.
Cohee retired the first two batters of the second inning. Samantha Witte then hit a towering pop-up that landed between second baseman Emily Boyle and right fielder Journey Pearson. Witte raced to second on the play, stole third and scored on Guy's single to left field for a 3-0 lead.
"Eight of our nine in the lineup are batting .390 or above," said Mardela head coach Kory Shiles, whose team defeated North Dorchester in last year's Bayside Conference championship — the last team to defeat the defending Class 1A state champion Eagles. "We have five" — Twilley, Wisk, Dorr, Donalds, Abby Campbell — "that are batting over .500. That to go with our phenomenal pitching ..."
Phenomenal indeed.
Coming into Thursday's game the Warriors had yielded just two runs in regular-season play — that to Colonel Richardson. Adkins (7-0) struck out eight and walked two. Then there's Twilley who has only given up one hit all season.
"Mardela played a great game," Hubbard said. "They made the plays when we put the ball in play. And Hayden pitched a great game."
North Dorchester got its only hit in the third, when Mackenzie Lewis beat out a spinning infield single up the third-base line. Cohee followed with a walk, but Adkins squelched the rally there, getting Kinsley Peters to ground out to short.
The closest the Eagles came to a second hit came in the fourth when Maggie Hubbard scorched a hard grounder went off first baseman Shockley that Shiles called an error. Adkins retired 11 of the final 12 batters she faced, surrendering a leadofff walk to Maddie Nagel in the seventh. Nagel, who was hit on the ankle with ball four, was lifted for a courtesy runner, who was thrown out trying to steal second.
Mardela extended its lead to 4-0 in the fourth. Guy and Wisk hit back-to-back two-out singles before Dorr singled to right, scoring Guy.
The Warriors put together another two-out rally in the fifth, but Cohee got a called third strike on Witte to end the inning.
"I thought Emilee pitched well," Hubbard said, whose starter gave up 11 hits, the last, an RBI double by Dorr that pushed Mardela's lead to 5-0 in the sixth and ended Cohee's day on the mound. "She gave up one walk. Not a bad performance. Can't ask a whole lot more out of your pitcher than that."
Twilley greeted reliever Jewels Vroman with an RBI single. The Warriors tacked on two more runs — both scoring on errors.
"I got a feeling we'll see them one more time, if not two more times," Shiles said of a potential rematch with the Eagles in the Bayside Conference championship and the Class 1A East Region I final.

title: Lions closer to finish line
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions closer to finish line

 April 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 590
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — One word has been on the collective minds of Queen Anne's County High's softball team all season. Finish."Our motto has been finish all year long," Lions head coach Aaron Stewart said. "We didn't finish last year. Coming into the season this year, one of my coaches just came up to me and said, 'You know the word of the year has to be finish.' And we're finishing right now."
Queen Anne's took a big step in putting itself in a position to finish atop the North Bayside Tuesday afternoon, using a nine-hit attack to back the pitching of Emily Hirschbock in a 6-1 victory over defending division champion North Dorchester.
The Lions (12-1 overall) moved into first place in the North at 4-1 and now hold the tiebreaker over the Eagles (11-2, 4-1) after beating them in their only head-to-head meeting of the season. Colonel Richardson (10-4, 4-2), which defeated Kent County by forfeit Tuesday, North Dorchester and Easton (6-4, 4-1) remain in contention but need help to overtake the Lions.
"The bats definitely came back today," said Stewart, who was puzzled after his team was limited to just five hits in last Tuesday's 4-1 loss to Colonel Richardson. "We hit the ball well. Opposite field, which is even better. I like to see opposite-field hitting. We practice that over and over and over again, to take that outside pitch and drive it to right field. And we executed it today."
The Lions did just that in the third inning, breaking a scoreless tie with three consecutive two-out, opposite-field hits for a 3-0 lead.
Morgan Gottleib worked a one-out walk against North Dorchester ace Emilee Cohee (5-2) and was advanced to second on Emily Hirschbock's sacrifice bunt. Cam Jacobi lined a single into right field to score Gottleib. Caroline Taylor (3 for 4) drilled a 1-0 offering into the right field corner for a double. Autumn Huber then drove another Cohee delivery the other way for a two-run triple.
North Dorchester scratched a run across in the top of the fourth. Maggie Hubbard (2 for 3) hit a leadoff single and scored four batters later, when freshman Journey Pearson lined a shot to center that Jacobi just missed making a spectacular leaping catch on for the third out of the inning.
That would be the lone run allowed by Hirschbock (7-0) who finished with a complete-game five-hitter, striking out four and walking four.
"I was just kind of thinking to attack every pitch," said Hirschbock, who retired nine of the last 11 batters she faced. "It's been a big thing for me to attack specifically the first batter. I feel like I did that pretty well tonight. I'm proud of myself for that.
"It's always nice pitching with the lead," Hirschbock said with a big smile. "My hitters hit and it was awesome."
Queen Anne's extended its lead in the fifth. Jacobi reached on a one-out error. Taylor dropped a bunt that Cohee fielded, but had to hold onto with no one covering first. Huber walked to load the bases. Abbie Denes singled to left field to plate Jacobi for a 4-1 lead. Cohee notched her seventh and final strikeout before Emily Rendulic singled to score Taylor and Huber for a 6-1 cushion.
"Tough day," North Dorchester head coach Carol Hubbard said. "They out-hit us. We had a few unfortunate things on the base paths. Not making excuses. They made the plays they had to make."
Maddie Nagel relieved Cohee, got an inning-ending strikeout, then held the Lions scoreless in the sixth despite yielding singles to Jacobi and Taylor.

 EASTON — The North Bayside softball championship.Defending division and Class 1A state champion North Dorchester was certainly cast among the favorites at the beginning of this season. Queen Anne's County and Colonel Richardson also figured to be right at the top.
Easton?
After a 1-3 start, some may have brushed the Warriors to the side, thinking this was a season of rebuilding, or at least readjusting under first-year head coach Ryan Brice. Well, Brice's bunch showed again Thursday afternoon they have adjusted just fine, notching their seventh win in eight games via a 10-0 five-inning shutout of Cambridge-South Dorchester.
Easton (8-4 overall) improved to 5-1 in the North, tied with Queen Anne's (13-1, 5-1) and North Dorchester (12-2, 5-1) — though the Eagles hold the tiebreaker over the Warriors, having won the only meeting between the two teams. Queen Anne's plays Easton on Tuesday.
"We're on a roll," Brice said. "Hopefully we can keep this going until next week because we have three straight (Queen Anne's, James M. Bennett, North Caroline), Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday."
Brice is also hoping Sammy Townsend can keep it going. With Lyle Roe not pitching this week due to an injury, Townsend (7-2) started all three games in the circle for the Warriors. The sophomore punctuated her week by throwing Easton's first shutout of the season, a three-hit gem that including 11 strikeouts — eight swinging — and no walks.
"Sammy did an amazing job, not only today, but the past three games that we had," Brice said. "Three-and-oh. She pitched amazing today with a shutout. I can't say enough about her. She's one of the best pitchers I've ever had the pleasure of coaching."
Townsend gave up a game-opening single to Enazajah Young, who raced to second when the ball bounced and hit center fielder Leigha Bosley in the throat. Townsend promptly struck out the next three, leaving Young, who stole third, stranded at third.
Camryn Russum singled sharply to left field with one out in the second, but was thrown out stealing by Warrior catcher Laillah Janes. Townsend fanned Evelyn Windsor to end the inning.
"I felt like my spins were really tight today, and the past couple of games," Townsend said. "I felt like this week I've pitched the best that I've pitched all season."
Townsend set the Vikings (6-7, 1-5) down in order in the third before Laila Insley reached with a bunt single down the third-base line to open the fourth. Townsend got Emma Robinson to pop out to short, watched Lainey Jones move Insley to second with a sacrifice bunt before striking out M'Kya Molock to end the frame.
The right-hander fanned the first two batters she faced in the fifth before Keyth Rodriguez smacked a comebacker off Townsend's glove. But Townsend finished the mercy-shortened game with her fourth inning-ending strikeout of the game.
"I knew my defense had me," Townsend said. "I feel like we have a set infield and outfield now, because I know in the beginning of the year we were all wishy-washy with who we were going to put where."
The Warriors took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first, when Mayah Wilkins (2 for 3) reached on an infield hit, dashed to third on a two-base throwing error on the play, and scored on a wild pitch.
Back-to-back, bases-loaded walks with two outs in the second extended that lead to 3-0.
Easton widened its advantage to 5-0 in the third. Townsend (2 for 3, two RBIs) roped a leadoff double into the left-field corner and scored on an error. Two batters later, Brynlee Buchkoski laced a triple to right that plated Janes. Buchkoski tried to score on a passed ball, but Viking catcher Lainey Jones threw to pitcher Robinson, who tagged out Buchkoski for the inning's final out.
The Warriors' lead ballooned to 10-0 in the fourth. After Bosley reached on an error, Wilkins doubled to left. Three batters later, Townsend lined a two-out, two-run single to right for a 7-0 lead. Janes and Gemma Vogel (2 for 3) followed with consecutive RBI singles. Robinson was relieved by Windsor, who gave up a bases-loaded walk to Isabelle Ludwig before getting two fly-ball outs to end the game.
NORTH DORCHESTER 9 NORTH CAROLINE 0
SHILOH — Senior Emilee Cohee hurled a no-hitter, striking out 10, as the Eagles improved to 12-2, 5-1. Freshmen Kinsley Peters and Journey Pearson each had two hits for North Dorchester.
BASEBALL
ST. MICHAELS 4 KENT COUNTY 2
ST. MICHAELS — Brock Grow tossed three innings of scoreless relief to earn the win, striking out seven of the nine batters he faced, as the Saints bounced back from Wednesday's 6-5 loss to Colonel Richardson.
Eli Wallace started for the Saints (14-1, 7-0), allowing two hits and one earned run. Jacob Bealefeld went 2 for 2 with a double and two RBIs, and Pearson Greenwood and Wallace each had a run-producing hit.
COLONEL 6 ST. MICHAELS 5
ST. MICHAELS — Jordan Regulski struck out seven over five innings and Jack Walls fanned six in two innings Wednesday, as Colonel Richardson handed the Saints their first loss of the season.
Manny Wallace and Regulski each had two hits for the Colonels. Walls, Brayden Dadds, Gavin Whitby and John Beaven had one each.
BOYS LACROSSE
EASTON 17, WICOMICO 2
EASTON — Jackson Weiland and Blake Royer each scored four goals Wednesday to lead the Warriors.
Logan Friend had a hat trick for Easton, Sam Noble scored twice, and Hudson Royer, Kyle Dyott, Landon Chaney and Grayson Buritsch had one apiece. Angel Fernandez won 12 faceoffs, and the defense of Jackson McKay, Nathan Lapp, Darren Foxwell, Colin Keenan and Charlie Beaufait limited the Indians to two goals.

title: Easton extends streak, but Eagles win title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton extends streak, but Eagles win title

 May 2, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1119
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Prior to the beginning of this season, Easton High first-year head softball coach Ryan Brice made a calendar."I just had us going to the Bayside championship game and states, 'cause I told them I believed in them that much, that they could do anything that they put their mind to," Brice said.
The Warriors continued their push toward turning Brice's calendar into reality Thursday, grinding out a 4-3 victory over North Caroline for their 10th win in 11 games. But Easton's title bid ended when North Dorchester earned a 5-1 victory over Colonel Richardson yesterday to clinch its second consecutive North Bayside championship.
The defending Class 1A state-champion Eagles (15-2 overall, 7-1 North Bayside) will meet unbeaten Mardela in a rematch of last year's conference championship on Tuesday at 5 p.m. at Salisbury University.
"We're doing what we need to do," Brice said after Easton improved to 11-4, 7-1 North Bayside, its lone division loss coming to North Dorchester on April 16.
Easton did just that on this sunny, wind-swept afternoon against a North Caroline team (8-8, 4-4) that threatened to end the Warriors' six-game win streak.
"They battled," North Caroline head coach Lee Hutchison said. "They played a good game. Both sides. We had a couple calls go against us there at the end that could have gone both ways. We get those calls and it's a tie game."
Tied 2-2, Isabelle Ludwig singled up the middle with one out in the Easton fourth. Ludwig advanced to second when Bulldog starting pitcher Katelyn Tribbitt walked Leigha Bosley. Mayah Wilkins (3 for 4) then stroked a single up the middle, scoring Ludwig from second for a 3-2 Warrior lead. Tribbitt ended the rally there, getting Lyla Roe to bounce into a fielder's choice before striking out Olivia Orrell.
Easton nudged its lead to 4-2 in the fifth. With one out, Tribbitt issued back-to-back walks to Laillah Janes and Gemma Vogel. Tribbitt was relieved by Anna Hutchison, who hit Brynlee Buchkoski with a pitch to load the bases before walking Ludwig, scoring courtesy runner Kristian Cherry. That would be the Warriors' final run, as Hutchison retired the next two batters, with third baseman Maddie Porter making a nice grab on Wilkins' low line drive to end the inning.
"They kept us in the game," Lee Hutchison said of his two pitchers. "They've been doing it all year. We just got to clean the defense up and get the key hits."
North Caroline threatened to tie the game in the top of the sixth.
Hatteras Ghrist led off with an infield hit, ripping a hard shot that Warrior third baseman Orrell made a nice backhanded stop on, but couldn't get the throw to first in time. Easton catcher Janes threw out Ghrist stealing before Hadley Eigenbrode dumped a single into shallow right field. Brooklyn Spencer came in as a courtesy runner for Eigenbrode.
Easton starting pitcher Sammy Townsend (10-2) got Jordyn Hunt to pop out to Wilkins at short for the second out. Alyssa Garlick followed by drilling an 0-1 pitch down the left-field line for a double, pushing Spencer to third. Porter smacked a comebacker off Townsend's glove that scored Spencer, making it a 4-3 game. Townsend then got Natellie Newman to bounce out to third for the final out, though North Caroline's coaching staff protested, arguing Newman beat Orrell's throw from third.
Gracie Calloway reached on a two-out error in the top of the seventh, but Townsend got Ghrist to pop out to second to end the game.
"It's been a long two weeks with the stretches of games that we've had," said Brice, whose team has gone 6-0 in that span. "I can't say enough about Sammy Townsend. She's an amazing pitcher. She's an amazing player. For her to be called on (in Wednesday's 8-6 come-from-behind win over James M. Bennett) in the first inning without warming up and finishing the game. She's matured these last two weeks and it shows."
Townsend gave up eight hits, struck out six and walked two.
North Caroline took a 2-0 lead in the third. Porter reached on a bad-hop single. Newman got on via an error. After walking Anna Hutchison, Tribbitt singled into center field, scoring Porter and Newman.
Easton answered in the bottom of the inning. Wilkins reached on a bunt single, stole second and third and scored when Roe jerked a double to left. Orrell singled. Townsend then sent a sacrifice fly to right that scored Roe with the tying run.
"We battled through our errors and everything, and we showed up at the plate," Townsend said. "I've definitely pitched better, but I've definitely pitched worse."
NORTH DORCHESTER 5, COL. RICHARDSON 1
SHILOH — Emilee Cohee pitched a three-hitter, striking out 12 and walking two as the Eagles clinched the North Bayside crown.
Mackenzie Lewis, Maggie Hubbard and Kinsley Peters each had two hits for North Dorchester.
QUEEN ANNE'S 19, CAMBRIDGE-SD 3
CAMBRIDGE — Abby Gunther went 4 for 4 and Morgan Gottleib was 3 for 4 with a homer to lead the Lions (16-2, 6-2).
Abbie Denes and Autumn Huber each drove in three runs for Queen Anne's, and Caroline Taylor, Camaryn Jacobi and Hannah Martin had multi-hit games.
Martin earned the win, allowing four hits over five innings, walking one, and striking out 10.
BASEBALL
NORTH DORCHESTER 6, WASHINGTON 5
PRINCESS ANNE — Nate Fraccaroli singled twice and doubled, driving in two runs, and Wes Windsor had three hits, an RBI and a run scored to lead the Eagles on Wednesday.
Starting pitcher John Boyle allowed four runs over four innings, striking out five for North Dorchester. TJ Leonard pitched three innings of scoreless relief, yielding one hit and fanning three, to earn the win.
Boyle had a hit, was walked twice and scored two runs. Vernon Price had two hits and stole four bases.
QUEEN ANNE'S 6, PARKSIDE 5
CENTREVILLE —Noah Palmer pitch 6 1/3 innings before Dalton Brown came on to earn the save Wednesday as the Lions topped the defending Class 2A state champions.
Palmer also went 2 for 3 with two RBIs for Queen Anne's. Bobby McCarthy (2 for 3)( knocked in a run, and Jacob Clough (two RBIs), Evan Keppler and Dulin Clark had one hit apiece.
GIRLS LACROSSE
SSPP 18, ST. MARK'S 5
EASTON — Senior Morgan Quade scored two goals and set up five others Wednesday to reach 200 goals and 400 assists for her career as the Sabres rolled to their 12th straight victory.
Sophomore Caroline Ewing netted seven goals and one assist for Saints Peter and Paul (12-1) and classmate Eryn Callahan had a hat trick and an assist. Kendall Kroniser and Emery Zimmerman each scored twice, and Samantha Murphy and Kate Sweeney had one goal apiece. Avery McCall finished with three assists and Emma Hainey had an assist. Goalie Kylie Kroniser made six saves and Veronica Pool had two stops.

title: DURRIE'S DEDICATION
author: Bill Haufe
content:
DURRIE'S DEDICATION

 July 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 831
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The late Durrie Hayes would have enjoyed the afternoon of May 28, 2024, his light mustache unable to conceal that Cheshire cat-like smile.A large collection of friends, former players and assistants gathered in a loose, elongated semicircle inside the right-field foul line at Easton High's softball field on that spring day fit for a doubleheader.
Soon bats would be swung, pitches hummed, ground and fly balls collected, and runs scored as part of the school's inaugural alumni softball game.
Not everyone had come to play, but all had come to catch the pregame that featured speeches thick on compliments, and the unveiling of the newly erected scoreboard behind the center-field fence in Hayes' honor. And those who knew him well can pretty much imagine Hayes' reaction once his eyes settled on his name emblazoned across the top of the scoreboard in big, bold orange letters outlined in white on a black background.
"I can just picture him smiling that little smile he had," said Casey (Dulin) Baynard, a star on Hayes' early teams and now a Warrior assistant. "I think he would have been very proud."
Dr. Ed Baker, the longtime umpiring legend who said, "Hayes was by far the best softball coach that I every umpired a game for," agreed.
"Durrie was a very humble person," Baker said of Hayes, who died April 2, 2020 at age 70 after a brief battle with cancer. "Naturally he would be very, very pleased and honored to see such a scoreboard. But he was never looking for his name to be in flashing lights."
Jay Cappa, an assistant during Hayes' 13 years at Easton, perhaps pegged the former head coach's reaction best.
"He would have said, 'Who'd a thunk it?'" Cappa said. "I do believe he would have said, 'Who'd a thunk it?'"
Actually, it was Byrd Dog Wheeler who first thunk Hayes be memorialized, initiating the drive for a scoreboard honoring the school's Hall of Fame coach four years ago.
"It's incredible what that guy did," said Wheeler, another longtime friend and one of the ceremony's speakers. "And that one run he had there; what the last eight years? Jeez Louise."
Hayes coached the Warriors from 1995-2007, compiling an impressive 232-46 record that included seven Bayside Conference championships, six regional titles and three state championships. Wedged in that 13-year stretch was an eight-year run (2000-07), where the Warriors went 162-18 that included a 23-0 season in 2004 — an unbeaten streak that was extended to 30 games the following year — three state championships and three state runner-up finishes.
"He put in all that time going to Little League girls softball games and travel team softball games, and talking to the parents and getting them involved, and getting them to buy into the program at such a young age," Wheeler said. "By the time they got up to ninth grade they were on track and knowing what to expect and ready to play. No one else did anything like that.
"One thing he couldn't say is that, 'There's others out there that deserve that a lot more than I do.' Not a chance he could say that," Wheeler added.
Well, now hold on there big dog.
There was in fact somebody who would have penciled himself into the leadoff spot to protest that very point — Hayes.
"It was always about the girls," Wheeler conceded. "It wasn't about Durrie Hayes."
Others could easily see Hayes lobbying for his players' names to be adorned atop the scoreboard, instead of his.
"I think deep down he would have been very honored," longtime friend Debbie Urry said. "But I think he would have been embarrassed because it should have gone to the girls. He was always about the girls. He never wanted that kind of attention. I think he would have been very humbled and surprised. And he would have given credit to all the girls he ever coached."
Jay Chance, who coached with Hayes at Easton and Chesapeake College, watched the skipper consistently direct praise his players' way.
"He never really made it all about him," said Chance, who presented Hayes during the induction ceremony for Easton High's inaugural Athletic Hall of Fame class in September 2019. "It was more important to make a difference in the girls' lives than it was to win a game. That's what I liked so much about him. Although on game day you would never know that [laughing]. On game day it was about winning."
Oh, and the fun Hayes would have had filling out the lineups for both teams in the alumni game.
"He definitely would have loved the alumni game that we had after that," Baynard said.
As the ceremony wrapped up, Cappa and Chance reminisced and joked about what Hayes' take would have been on this big to-do.
"Jay said, 'Watch it. He's libel to send down a lightning bolt,'" Cappa said laughing. "I told Jay, 'He's not going to do it 'cause they're going to play a softball game. He ain't going to ruin the softball game.' He said, 'Yeah, I guess you're right.'"
